universalControls: Authority follows the approved reporting line and documented delegation, not seniority or a job title alone.
Board authority is collective unless a valid resolution expressly delegates a defined power.
Executive Director is the overall management authority and reports to the Board.
Departmental heads exercise only authority expressly delegated by the Executive Director.
Sub-delegation is prohibited unless the written delegation permits it.
Every approval/signature must be attributable to the actor's active appointment and capacity at the time.
No self-approval; incompatible preparation, review, approval, signing and release duties must be separated.
Acting appointments require written scope, start/end dates and approving authority.
A person with multiple roles must select the capacity relevant to the action; roles do not combine automatically.
The matrix does not replace the Constitution, law, bank mandate, procurement policy or Board resolutions.
The Executive Director also holds the permanent employee office of Board Secretary; each action must use the selected capacity and applicable authority independently.
Board Members serve four-year terms, renewable once, with a maximum tenure of eight years; this tenure limit does not apply to the permanent employee Board Secretary office.
The next senior Director represents the Executive Director during absence only within the Constitution and a recorded acting scope; no permanent succession is inferred.
IRPA has existing authorised bank accounts and signatories; current bank mandates, not job titles or this matrix, determine bank execution.

The Executive Director reviews and releases job descriptions to the Administrator; the Administrator assigns and releases each approved description to the respective delegate without expanding its authority.
Volunteer engagement is distinct from employment and conveys no implied financial, procurement, banking, administrator, security, research or production authority.
